bear_case.title: The stopgap budget freezes the programs the growth stories depend on
bear_case.description: The continuing resolution runs to Dec 11 and leaves the Pentagon on $838.5B versus a $1.5T FY27 request; it blocks new starts for 150+ programs, Golden Dome has no base topline (most funding came via the 2025 reconciliation bill), F-15EX starts FY27 with $115M of $2.65B requested and the $54.6B DAWG drone line cannot begin; the base budget may not clear until spring 2027.
bear_case.counter: Congress has historically backfilled priority programs after a CR, and the reconciliation route could still deliver Golden Dome funding.

bear_case.title: Public-market valuations remain stretched
bear_case.description: A broad risk-off on Oct 30 (QQQ down ~4% intraday) cut Palantir ~3.9% on Lang & Schwarz and hit high-beta drone names; Palantir trades at a premium multiple (~80x+ forward earnings last confirmed) after a ~59% three-month run and the S&P Aerospace & Defense sub-index sits near 32x forward earnings versus roughly 20x for the S&P 500 — a premium the sector has to keep earning.
bear_case.counter: Palantir's 92.8% revenue growth and rising EPS estimates are far faster than higher-multiple software peers.

bear_case.title: Private-market valuations are drawing bubble comparisons of their own
bear_case.description: Early-stage rounds price at 17x-50x revenue, Anduril's ~$100B primary round remains unconfirmed (the Oct 13 tender prices it at ~$90B), and the Bank for International Settlements has compared the sector's pricing to the AI-infrastructure buildout it already calls bubble-like.

bear_case.title: The Pentagon's drone competitions keep favoring private newcomers over listed pure-plays
bear_case.description: Gauntlet II leaders Neros and Perennial Autonomy won real orders (Neros: ~$100M for 14,000+ FPV drones on Oct 1), while Red Cat's Teal Drones, Ondas's Ascent Aerosystems and Kratos all missed the top five.

bear_case.title: Contract wins and beats aren't rescuing the pure-play stocks
bear_case.description: AeroVironment beat Q2 estimates ($0.59 vs. $0.22 EPS) and won a $464.8M laser award yet trades near $127 (~48% down YTD); Ondas reported $165M of new orders on Oct 7 and a FEMA counter-drone tie-in on Oct 30, yet sits near $6.3 (-36% YTD); Red Cat is ~$4.56 (-43% YTD). Drone names fell 6-10% on Oct 30 alone.
bear_case.counter: The ~$232 consensus target implies substantial upside if backlog converts to earnings.

bear_case.title: Rheinmetall's rebound is fragile — execution, not backlog, sets the stock
bear_case.description: The rebound to ~EUR1,038 (Oct 30) still leaves it far below the ~EUR1,922 high, and Berenberg's Hold (target EUR1,020) cites valuation and a lack of recent large orders; delivery delays, negative operating free cash flow and the F126 loss make the Q3 results (expected Nov 5) a binary test.
bear_case.counter: Deutsche Bank (target €1,800) expects >40% Q3 revenue growth, and CEO and board-linked insider purchases in late September/October suggest management sees the earlier de-rating as overdone.

bear_case.title: UK fiscal strain is now a risk for UK defence names
bear_case.description: BAE fell ~4.1-4.7% on Oct 6 (~21% below its March peak) after Defence Secretary Healey resigned over slow spending and reports the 3%-of-GDP spending review could slip to autumn 2027; hitting the NATO target would cost roughly £10B a year extra. The Oct 28 Autumn Budget outcome for defence could not be confirmed this week, so the funding question should be treated as unresolved.
bear_case.counter: Roughly half of BAE's revenue is U.S.-linked and the order book is multi-year, so near-term revenue is less exposed than the share price implies.
